meta.title: Bayer CropScience methomyl residue treater (Institute, West Virginia), as described by the CSB
meta.source_document: U.S. Chemical Safety Board, Investigation Report No. 2008-08-I-WV (January 2011): Pesticide Chemical Runaway Reaction Pressure Vessel Explosion, Bayer CropScience, LP, Institute, West Virginia, August 28, 2008. https://www.csb.gov/assets/1/20/Bayer_Report_Final.pdf
meta.page_convention: p. = the report's printed page number; Fig = the report's figure number.
meta.tag_convention: The report names instrument types but no instrument or valve tag numbers for the residue treater, so every tag here is ASSIGNED by this project (ISA-5.1 letters, loop numbers 101-110) and marked assigned_tag: true. Equipment identifiers RT-1, E-1, E-2, E-3, P-1 are assigned the same way. Nothing here is the plant's own numbering.
meta.scope: The residue treater and its recirculation, heating, cooling, vent and discharge systems as drawn in Fig 10 (p. 29) and described on pp. 27-32 and 38-40. Upstream (methomyl synthesis, flashers) and downstream (alternate fuel tank, flare) are battery limits.
meta.not_a_drawing_of_record: Built from a public investigation report to show the method. Not the plant's design, not reviewed by anyone who operated it.

facts.relief_basis: methomyl concentration not to exceed 1.0 percent

units.name: Vent condenser
units.source: Fig 10; p. 28 (vent piping prone to blockages)

streams.name: Discharge to the auxiliary (alternate) fuel tank
Condenser vent to the process vent (flare)
Cooling water (80 C) through the cooler

instruments.description: Residue treater temperature (as plotted in Fig 11)
instruments.open_question: The report says the control system monitored both the bulk liquid and the recirculation loop (p. 28) but does not say which one Fig 11 plots or Fig 10's transmitter measures.

instruments.description: Second temperature measurement (bulk liquid or recirculation loop; see TI-104)
instruments.source: p. 28 (text only; not drawn in Fig 10)

instruments.description: Indicated steam flow to the heater

final_elements.source: Fig 10; pp. 30-31 (set in manual, closed during startup; automatic once samples confirmed)

final_elements.description: Discharge control valve to the alternate fuel tank
final_elements.source: Fig 10; p. 28 (automatic level control); p. 32 (kept in manual, batch transfers)

final_elements.description: Steam flow valve to the heater (Fig 10: Temperature Control Valve)

manual_valves.description: Steam block valve, heater steam supply
manual_valves.source: Fig 10; p. 70 (found closed instead of fully open); Fig 20, p. 72

relief_devices.source: Fig 10; Fig 11 label (relief valve open, 44 psig, 22:27)

controllers.description: Automatic level control at about 50 percent
controllers.as_operated: kept in manual; level allowed to rise to the upper fill limit and transferred in batches (p. 32)

controllers.description: Split-range temperature control: heats through the heater (steam valve and heater-leg valve) during startup; at the setpoint it closes the steam valve and moves recirculation from the heater to the cooler
controllers.as_found: incorrectly programmed: changing from heating to cooling closed the recirculation valves to both the heater and the cooler, blocking all recirculation flow (p. 39, footnote 29; CSB: not causal)

interlocks.cause: TI-104 below the minimum temperature setpoint
interlocks.as_found: bypassed on the night of the incident, based on experience with the heater (p. 69)

interlocks.cause: PI-101 at or above the maximum pressure setpoint

limits.what: Minimum fill before starting the pump
Methomyl in the vessel before feeding
Sample before re-heating if cooled below
Methomyl concentration with runaway risk on heating

events_2008_08_28.what: Recirculation pump started; level about 30 percent; temperature 60-65 C; pressure 22 psig
Temperature begins rising about 0.6 C per minute
Level 51 percent; recirculation flow drops to zero
High pressure alarm at the work station (approximately)

people: Two employees died: one at the scene, the second 41 days later. Six volunteer firefighters and two contractors were treated for possible toxic chemical exposure (p. 1). This model exists to show how published operating data and a drawing can be checked against each other; it does not judge the operators.
